name: What is the difference between a built-in, floating, and fold-down shower bench?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a built-in, floating, and fold-down shower bench?

acceptedAnswer.text: A built-in shower bench is permanently framed, waterproofed, and tiled directly into your shower walls and floor. A floating bench is securely anchored into wall framing without legs touching the floor, while a fold-down seat attaches to reinforced wall backing and tucks away when not in use. Freestanding benches are movable stools, usually made of teak or water-resistant materials, that require no construction. Built-in styles offer maximum stability and integrated storage, while fold-down or freestanding seats save floor space in smaller walk-in showers.
acceptedAnswer.description: Built-in benches are permanently tiled structures, floating benches mount to the wall with open floor space beneath, and fold-down seats collapse against the wall to save room.
